_README: Industry events / semiconductor conferences that can move watchlist names via product announcements, roadmap disclosures, or competitive read-through. The morning routine (CLAUDE.md) refreshes dates and 'watch' notes via web search each run and adds newly-announced events. 'tickers' = watchlist symbols with direct or read-through exposure. 'confidence': confirmed (dates verified) | approx (typical timing, verify) | rumored. Dates are ISO YYYY-MM-DD, event-local. Not investment advice.

events.name: Rosenblatt 6th Annual Technology Summit: The Age of AI (Part II)
events.watch: Added 2026-08-05: broker-hosted virtual tech summit (Part I ran Jun 9-10; Part II is Aug 17-18). Watchlist relevance is narrow but dated and specific: **AAOI presents in a fireside chat on Tue Aug 18 at 11:00am ET, with Stefan Murry (CFO and Chief Strategy Officer)** — announced 2026-08-04. Calibrate expectations: this is a sell-side investor event, not a technical venue, so it produces commentary and guidance colour rather than product disclosure. Its value is timing — it falls 12 days after AAOI's Q2 print (Aug 6) and lands in the middle of the live FCC/Chinese-optical-transceiver-ban story that moved AAOI +17% on 08-04, so it is the first scheduled opportunity for management to be asked directly about import-ban exposure, 800G/1.6T capacity at the Pearland expansion, and CPO timing. A recording is posted to the company IR site afterwards. Re-verified 2026-08-06: AAOI's fireside chat with Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO) is confirmed for **Tue Aug 18, 11:00am ET**; other confirmed participants now visible include Rambus, Arteris and Extreme Networks (none on the watchlist). The timing note sharpens: **AAOI reports Q2 TODAY (Aug 6, 4:30pm ET)**, so by Aug 18 management will have both the print and twelve more days of FCC-rule developments behind them — this is the first venue where the guide and the import-ban exposure get questioned together. 11 days out. **Re-checked 2026-08-06 midday: no change to the agenda since the morning pass — Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO) confirmed Tue Aug 18, 11:00am ET, other visible participants Rambus, Arteris, Extreme Networks (none on the watchlist).** The one thing that changes between now and then is tonight: **AAOI's Q2 print lands at 4:30pm ET today**, so this fireside becomes either a victory-lap venue or a damage-control venue depending on a result that is still ~5 hours out at this cutoff. 11 days out. **Updated 2026-08-06 evening run (~17:30 BRT / 20:30 UTC) — the variable this entry has been waiting on has resolved: AAOI's Q2 printed at 4:30pm ET today and it was a beat with a large guide-up.** Revenue **$191.9M** (+86% YoY, +27% QoQ, above the $180-198M guide and the ~$190.5M consensus), **non-GAAP EPS +$0.06 against ~$0.03 consensus** — the first non-GAAP profitable quarter, versus a -$8.8M non-GAAP loss a year ago — and **Q3 guided to $255-290M revenue** (midpoint +44% QoQ) with non-GAAP net income $10.1-24.0M. Datacenter revenue **$107.7M, more than double** the year-ago $44.8M; 800G volume **more than doubled sequentially**; management says demand **outpaces production capacity through mid-2027** and guides capacity from ~200,000 units/month now to **~650,000 units/month of 800G and 1.6T by year-end**. **What this does to the Aug 18 fireside: it turns it from an adjudication venue into a follow-up venue, and sharpens what is actually still unanswered.** The print did NOT address the FCC/Chinese-transceiver import rule, China exposure, CPO, or datacenter customer concentration — none of those appear in the release — so Stefan Murry (CFO/CSO, Tue Aug 18, 11:00am ET) is now the first scheduled venue where the import-ban exposure gets questioned against a printed quarter and a $1bn+ FY26 framing. The two questions the numbers themselves raise and the release does not answer: (a) **gross margin did not expand on a 27% sequential revenue increase** — GAAP 27.7% (down from 30.3% YoY) and non-GAAP 29.8%, at the low end of the 29-30% guide, with **adjusted EBITDA still slightly negative at -$0.5M**; and (b) the **share count**, which goes from 81.6M weighted-average basic in Q2 to **92.8M assumed for the Q3 EPS guide**, alongside cash building from $216.0M at YE2025 to $449.4M at Q1 to **$508.8M** now. 12 days out.

events.name: Hot Chips 2026 (IEEE Symposium on High-Performance Chips)
events.watch: Re-checked 2026-07-31: no material change since the 07-30 pass — official program still shows speaker names attached to essentially all previously-listed talks. NVDA (5 talks): Vera CPU (Jonathon Evans & Polychronis Xekalakis); Rubin GPU 'Driving the Era of Agentic AI' (Manas Mandal, Rajballav Dash & Ravi Manyam); BlueField-4 (Idan Burstein); Spectrum-X multiplane networking (Gilad Shainer); the heterogeneous GPU-LPU design is titled 'Think Fast' LPU accelerator (Igor Arsovski & Santosh Raghavan). AVGO (1 talk): Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC (Hemal Shah). AMD (4 talks, non-watchlist but competitive read-through): MI400 architecture (Alan Smith & Maiyuran Subramaniam), MI400 system architecture (Steve Scott, David Riddoch & Krishna Doddapaneni), secure SoC (Jaideep Dastidar & Thomas To), Versal RF (Jeff Cuppett). Keynote confirmed: Daniel Rosenband (Waymo), 'Compute in Motion: Challenges of Autonomous Driving.' Second keynote still unnamed. Two tutorials now have topics (memory technology & AI data requirements; RISC-V standards and adoption) but speakers still TBD. MRVL, TSM, GFS: still NO confirmed talks in the official program — read-through for those three remains indirect (foundry/interconnect layer under NVDA/AVGO/AMD silicon), unchanged from prior note. Also present, non-watchlist context: Google 8th-gen TPU, Meta MTIA. Re-verified 2026-08-03: dates confirmed Aug 23-25 at Memorial Auditorium, Stanford (plus online); program still lists two tutorials, two keynotes and ~25 architect presentations from AMD, Intel, NVIDIA, Google and others. The SECOND KEYNOTE REMAINS UNNAMED — the one open slot in the program and the only place a genuine surprise can still enter. No change to any watchlist-relevant talk since the 07-31 pass. Re-checked again 2026-08-03 evening: second keynote still unnamed, no program changes. New: @firstadopter (tae kim, Tier 1) confirmed on 08-01 that he is attending, so expect first-hand written coverage of the NVDA Vera/Rubin/BlueField-4/Spectrum-X talks rather than only the official program. Re-verified 2026-08-04 morning against the official program page: dates and every watchlist-relevant talk unchanged (NVDA x4 — Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, BlueField-4, Spectrum-X multiplane; AVGO x1 — Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC; still no MRVL/TSM/GFS talks), Rosenband/Waymo keynote confirmed, and the SECOND KEYNOTE IS STILL UNNAMED — five consecutive passes with that slot open, which by now is itself the signal: either a late-breaking announcement or a low-key fill. 19 days out. Re-checked 2026-08-04 midday: official program unchanged again — dates Aug 23-25 at Memorial Auditorium (plus online), two keynotes / two tutorials / ~25 architect talks, every watchlist-relevant talk identical (NVDA x4, AVGO x1 Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC, still no MRVL/TSM/GFS), and the SECOND KEYNOTE IS STILL UNNAMED — a sixth consecutive pass with that slot open, 19 days out. Treat it as a low-information slot now rather than a pending catalyst; it will be re-checked but will not be re-narrated each run unless it fills. Re-checked 2026-08-05 morning: seventh consecutive pass, second keynote still unnamed, dates and all watchlist-relevant talks unchanged — logged as a stamp only, per the standing note not to re-narrate this slot until it fills. 18 days out. Re-verified 2026-08-05 midday against the official program: dates unchanged (Aug 23-25, Memorial Auditorium, Stanford), Rosenband/Waymo keynote confirmed for Mon Aug 24 2:15pm, and the **second keynote is still unnamed — eighth consecutive pass**. Logged as a stamp only, per the standing note. No watchlist-relevant talk changed. 18 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-05 evening run against the official ADVANCE PROGRAM page (not just the landing page) — and this pass found real new content, the first in several runs.** The second keynote is still unnamed (ninth consecutive pass — stamp only, per the standing note), and the Rosenband/Waymo keynote is confirmed for Mon Aug 24. What is NEW: **(1) Tutorial 1 (Memory Technology, Sun Aug 23) now has a published topic list, and it explicitly includes HBF in AI compute**, alongside AI memory demands, evolving memory architectures, HBM evolution, advanced packaging and 3D DRAM accelerators. That matters because it makes Hot Chips the *second* venue in three weeks to give High Bandwidth Flash a formal slot — FMS 2026 (Aug 4-6) is where SK hynix and SanDisk published the standard spec through OCP, and Hot Chips is where the architecture community interrogates it. A tier that gets a tutorial at the architects' conference is being treated as an architecture question, not a marketing one. **(2) SAMSUNG is on the program and was not previously listed here — with an LPDDR5X-PIM talk and an HBM-evolution talk.** The LPDDR5X-PIM part is the same industry-first Samsung just unveiled at FMS on Aug 4, so the memory complex carries a continuous thread from FMS into Hot Chips; Samsung is the largest single weight in EWY, hence the ticker addition. **(3) INTC is now a directly-presenting watchlist name and has been added to the ticker list** — Intel has three talks: Core Series 3 (Wildcat Lake), Diamond Rapids Xeon, and **Crescent Island, its GPU for agentic AI inference**, which is the one with thesis relevance. Memory-complex tickers (000660.KS/SKHY/MU/DRAM/DISK) added for the tutorial-1 HBF/HBM/3D-DRAM read-through. Unchanged: NVDA x5 (Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, BlueField-4, Spectrum-X, 'Think Fast' LPU), AVGO x1 (Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC), AMD x4, Google 8th-gen TPU, Meta MTIA, and **still no confirmed MRVL / TSM / GFS talks** — those three remain indirect read-through only. Also on the program as non-watchlist context: IBM Z/LinuxONE, Arm, Fujitsu, SambaNova, Cerebras, Microsoft, OpenAI, Mojo Vision. 18 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-06 morning against the official advance program — and this pass found real new content again.** The second keynote is **still unnamed (tenth consecutive pass — stamp only, per the standing note)**, and Rosenband/Waymo remains confirmed for **Mon Aug 24, 2:15-3:15pm PDT**. What is NEW: **Tutorial 1 (Memory Technology, Sun Aug 23, 9:00am-12:30pm) now carries NAMED SPEAKERS, and the roster is the memory complex itself** — Jim Handy (Objective Analysis), **Raghu Sreeramaneni (MICRON)**, **Sangwook Han (SAMSUNG)**, **Jaesik Lee (SK HYNIX)**, Sudeep Bhoja (d-Matrix) and Aayush Ankit (Meta), covering AI infrastructure memory demands, HBM evolution and 3D DRAM accelerators alongside the previously-logged HBF slot. Last pass this tutorial had a topic list and no speakers; it now has all three memory makers presenting in the same 3.5-hour session, which makes Hot Chips the venue where the four incompatible FMS answers (HBF, zHBM, IMTE, CMX) get argued in front of the architecture community rather than the trade press. **Tutorial 2 (RISC-V, Sun Aug 23, 1:45-5:00pm) is also now populated** — Krste Asanovic (SiFive), Gordan Markus (Canonical), **Frans Sijstermans (NVIDIA — GPU interoperability)** and Thomas Roecker (Infineon); the NVIDIA slot there is a sixth NVDA appearance on the program and the only one about someone else's ISA. Unchanged: NVDA x5 (Vera CPU, Rubin GPU, BlueField-4, Spectrum-X, 'Think Fast' LPU), AVGO x1 (Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC), INTC x3 (Wildcat Lake, Diamond Rapids, Crescent Island), Samsung LPDDR5X-PIM + HBM evolution, AMD x4, and **still no confirmed MRVL / TSM / GFS talks**. 17 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-06 evening against the official advance program — no change since the morning pass.** The second keynote is **still unnamed (eleventh consecutive pass — stamp only, per the standing note)**; Rosenband/Waymo remains the only named keynote. Tutorial 1 (Memory Technology, Sun Aug 23) speaker roster confirmed unchanged and now with talk titles attached — Jim Handy (Objective Analysis) 'Memory: Feeding AI's voracious hunger for data', **Raghu Sreeramaneni (MICRON) 'Evolving memory architectures for AI'**, **Sangwook Han (SAMSUNG) on HBM base die**, **Jaesik Lee (SK HYNIX) on advanced packaging for HBM**, plus Sudeep Bhoja (d-Matrix) and Aayush Ankit (Meta) on 3D DRAM accelerators. Note the SK hynix title in particular: **advanced packaging**, which is exactly the shared constraint the FMS week converged on rather than the tier branding. Tutorial 2 (RISC-V) unchanged. NVDA x5, INTC x3, AVGO x1, Samsung x2, AMD, and **still no confirmed MRVL / TSM / GFS talks**. 17 days out.

events.name: SPIE Optics + Photonics 2026
events.watch: Added 2026-08-03: dates verified against SPIE's own listing — conferences Aug 23-27, exhibition Aug 25-27, courses Aug 23-26. Calibrate expectations: this is SPIE's RESEARCH-tier optics meeting (optical engineering, nanophotonics, optoelectronic materials, quantum), NOT the datacom/telecom product venue — ECOC (Sep 20-24) and OFC (Mar 2027) remain the real catalyst windows for CPO, 1.6T transceivers and InP-laser roadmaps. Value here is early technical signal on InP/photonic-substrate materials and packaging that shows up as product 12-24 months later, which matters given the InP substrate shortage now documented in the SIVE file (AXT/Lumentum LTA to 2031, Lumentum CEO citing a >30% demand-supply gap). Runs exactly concurrent with Hot Chips 2026 (Aug 23-25) — the same week carries both the compute-silicon and the photonics-research read. Re-verified 2026-08-05 evening: dates and structure unchanged against SPIE's own program page — Aug 23-27 at the San Diego Convention Center, exhibition Aug 25-27, courses Aug 23-26, ~45 conferences and ~2,000 presentations, with plenaries flagged on sustainability and AI/ML. No watchlist company is a named plenary speaker, which is consistent with the research-tier framing above; treat this as a materials/packaging listening post rather than a catalyst date. The concurrency note stands and is now sharper: Aug 23-25 carries Hot Chips (compute silicon, incl. an HBF tutorial) and SPIE O+P (photonics research) in the same window.

events.name: SEMICON Taiwan 2026
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: major Asia-Pacific fab-equipment/WFE show, ~5 days after AI Infra Summit and ~2.5 weeks before ECOC — same September AI-infra/semi catalyst cluster. 2026 program spans 13 themes incl. AI chips, advanced packaging, 3DIC, chiplets, heterogeneous integration; watch for TSMC capacity/pricing commentary and equipment-order read-through. Re-verified 2026-08-04 against SEMI's own release: dates confirmed **Sep 2-4 at Nangang Halls 1 & 2**, with the **conference program running wider than the exhibition — Aug 31 through Sep 4**, so the first TSMC/supply-chain commentary can land two days before the show floor opens. Record scale this year: **1,300+ exhibitors and 4,300+ booths (both all-time highs), 100,000+ attendees from 65 countries.** Named themes now include **silicon photonics** alongside AI chips, advanced packaging and quantum — which makes this a secondary read for the SIVE/SOI optics chain, not only a TSM/GFS event, though ECOC (Sep 20-24) remains the real optics catalyst. 29 days out. **Re-verified 2026-08-06: dates unchanged (Sep 2-4, Nangang) and the OPENING KEYNOTE IS NOW NAMED — Amin Vahdat, SVP & Chief Technologist of AI and Infrastructure at GOOGLE**, on Google's view of AI infrastructure and the semiconductor ecosystem. That is a notable choice for a Taiwanese fab-equipment show: the opening slot goes to a hyperscaler's infrastructure architect rather than to a foundry or WFE executive, which is the demand side setting the agenda for the supply side. Vahdat is also the TPU/networking lineage at Google, so watch for anything on custom-silicon volumes, optics and packaging demand that reads through to TSM/GFS capacity and to the optics chain. Eight named themes this year (advanced manufacturing, heterogeneous integration, compound semiconductors, auto chips, smart manufacturing, sustainability, semiconductor cybersecurity, workforce) — compound semiconductors keeps the secondary InP/photonics read alive. 27 days out.

events.name: AI Infra Summit 2026
events.watch: Speaker list expanded to 400+ as of 2026-07-27 scan (8,000+ attendees, 300+ sessions, 8 stages) across 5 tracks: Compute, Data Movement, Physical AI, Data & Models, AI Data Center. Named speakers now include Lip-Bu Tan (CEO, Intel) and Dave Lazovsky (EVP, Marvell) on the main stage, plus Jeff Dean (Google), Kripa Krishnan (VP, Meta AI Infrastructure) — direct read-through for INTC and MRVL specifically, not just the thematic complex, alongside NVDA/AVGO/WULF/META exposure already logged. Falls 5 days before ECOC 2026, inside the same September AI-infra catalyst window.

events.name: ECOC 2026 (European Conference on Optical Communication)
events.watch: THE optics event for the small-caps: CPO (co-packaged optics), 800G/1.6T transceivers, EML/DFB laser and InP-substrate progress. Direct catalyst window for Sivers (CPO lasers) and Soitec (photonics substrates); DSP/optics read-through for MRVL & AVGO. Lumentum/Coherent disclosures here reset the whole InP supply picture.

events.name: OCP Global Summit 2026 (Open Compute Project)
events.watch: Hyperscaler datacenter standards — rack power/cooling, networking fabrics, custom silicon, optics adoption. Meta is a core OCP driver (capex read-through); networking/optics read-through for AVGO & MRVL; datacenter-infrastructure read-through for WULF's HPC-conversion thesis.

events.name: SEMICON West 2026
events.watch: Dates confirmed 2026-07-22 via the official SEMI organizer site (Pre-Show Day Mon Oct 12, show floor Oct 13-15). Fab-equipment/WFE industry event, almost exactly overlapping the existing OCP Global Summit (Oct 12-15, San Jose) — same catalyst week. Relevant to TSM (leading-edge capacity/pricing commentary) and GFS (specialty-foundry, onshoring/CHIPS Act positioning).

events.name: IEDM 2026 (72nd IEEE International Electron Devices Meeting)
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: premier device-physics/process-tech conference, theme 'Devices at the Heart of the Intelligence Revolution.' Expect next-node transistor (GAA/CFET) and advanced-packaging/substrate papers directly relevant to Soitec's SOI/substrate roadmap plus TSM/INTC/GFS process roadmaps. Detailed accepted-paper program not yet released; dates flagged 'subject to change' by some listings — verify closer to the event.

events.name: CES 2027
events.watch: Consumer + edge-AI keynotes; NVIDIA typically opens with a roadmap/keynote. Broad AI-infrastructure tone-setter for the year. 60th-anniversary edition.

events.name: OFC 2027 (Optical Fiber Communication Conference & Exposition)
events.watch: Added 2026-07-30: the largest global optics show — the semiannual bookend to ECOC for CPO/transceiver/InP-laser roadmap disclosures (1.6T/3.2T transceivers, co-packaged optics), directly feeding the Sivers/Soitec thesis.

events.name: NVIDIA GTC 2027
events.watch: NVIDIA's flagship — next-gen architecture (post-Rubin) roadmap, networking (NVLink/Spectrum), and increasingly CPO/optics partners. The single biggest AI-infra catalyst of the year; read-through across the entire watchlist, especially the optics chain if NVDA advances co-packaged optics.
